holidays.name: Red Planet Day
holidays.description: A day for looking up at Mars and celebrating the dusty, rusty neighbor we keep sending robots to visit. Space fans mark it with Mars-themed snacks, stargazing and rover trivia.
holidays.origin: The day marks the 1964 launch of NASA's Mariner 4 on November 28. That probe went on to make the first successful flyby of Mars and sent back the first close-up photos of another planet.
holidays.funFact: Mariner 4 returned just 21 photos of Mars. Each one took hours to send back to Earth, and early on, scientists hand-colored a printout of the data with pastels because they couldn't wait for the computers.

holidays.name: National French Toast Day
holidays.description: An unofficial celebration of turning stale bread into a breakfast star. Dunk it in egg and milk, griddle it until golden, then pile on syrup, powdered sugar, fruit or whatever else you like.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on the late-November breakfast calendar.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, French toast is far older than France's claim to it. Recipes for soaked and fried bread date back to ancient Rome, and in France it is called 'pain perdu,' or 'lost bread,' because it rescues bread that would otherwise be wasted.
